question.body:
The graph of $f$ passes through $(3,6)$ and $f'(x)=(1+e^x)/x^2$.

(a) Write the tangent line at $x=3$ and use it to approximate $f(3.1)$.

(b) Starting at $x=3$ with step size $0.05$, use Euler's method to approximate $f(3.1)$. Use $f''$ to explain why this estimate is less than $f(3.1)$.

(c) Use $integral_3^3.1 f'(x) dif x$ to evaluate $f(3.1)$.
question.solution:
(a) $f'(3)=(1+e^3)/9 approx 2.3426$. The tangent line is
$y-6=(1+e^3)/9(x-3)$,
so $f(3.1) approx 6.2343$.

(b) Euler's method gives
$f(3.05) approx 6+f'(3)(0.05) approx 6.1171$,
$f(3.1) approx 6.1171+f'(3.05)(0.05) approx 6.2360$.
Also
$f''(x)=((x-2)e^x-2)/x^3>0$ on $[3,3.1]$. The graph is concave up, so the Euler tangent-line estimates lie below it.

(c)
$f(3.1)=6+integral_3^3.1 (1+e^x)/x^2 dif x approx 6.2378$.
